reason:
This is an error stop with state blocked at Worktree-Create, step 1 of 8. The cause named is that a held board lock deferred the push of the board commit, so the board was still ahead of origin. The way forward it names is "run `lym board sync`, then re-run the verb". That cause no longer holds. I checked each fact read-only at 10:30:
- `git -C _bolt status -sb` now reads `main...origin/main`, so the board is no longer ahead.
- `ls-remote origin main` is 4f6af5b1, the same as local HEAD. The commit 262c5f17 that the case brief found local-only is now an ancestor of origin/main (`merge-base --is-ancestor` exits 0). The detached board sync, pid 3861142, has exited, and its push and a later one (4f6af5b1) both landed.
- The records side, 9744e0d0, is on origin main-weft, as the case brief shows.
- No push-lock holder is running. pid 3750437 is gone, and the .weft lock files are the empty flock files from October.
- The board entry already has owner_machine neve, so the claim itself is recorded.
Both stops of this kind, attempt 1's and this one, came from push contention. Other writers moved origin main between the read and the push, as the two "cannot lock ref ... expected" rejections in trace a223821f5cd36e91 show. Each time the deferred sync landed afterwards. That is transient contention, not a defect in the run or in the task, and nothing is left to sync. Re-running Worktree-Create from a level board is the step the error message itself prescribes. If the claim stops a third time on the same board reason, the race is not transient and should go to the parent.
